blocks.x: HPC scheduling reformulated, cluster utilization up 19 points and the paper backlog from compute queues cut by two-thirds
Identity withheld, a research university whose cluster was world-class and whose queue was world-famous among its PhD students. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline semester measured the queue: 58% average utilization with usage spiking per deadline season, 400-job waitlists on the GPU partitions, and three published papers whose reviewers asked why results took nine months to produce.
Scheduling ran on first-come-first-served with manual exceptions; fairness lived in the queue order, and priority negotiations happened in corridor conversations.

We reformulated the scheduler: job shapes profiled from real history, backfill and priority decomposition producing schedules reproducible seed-by-seed, burst capacity on cloud for deadline seasons with data locality respected, and the fairness policy written as code the community reviews openly. The corridor negotiation became a configuration change.
